newsitem.title: UK: UTA Europe to close N.Irish plant.
newsitem.headline: UTA Europe to close N.Irish plant.

text.p: U.S. car components firm, United Technologies Automotive Ltd is to close its plant in Londonderry in Northern Ireland, it announced on Tuesday.
The company, which makes wiring harnesses for a range of cars, employs some 600 people in the high-unemployment Bogside district.
"It is with regret that the company is proposing to close down its Derry plant over the next several weeks," UTA Europe said in a statement.
"For a number of years, considerable effort and investment has been expended to make this operation a success.
"Several factors, not least the ever-increasing pressure on prices, prevented the desired outcome and resulted instead in substantial losses during recent years."
The firm, which also has factories in Spain, Portugal and Hungary, manufactures wiring for car firms that include PSA (Peugeot) and Jaguar.
Community leaders in Londonderry said that the job losses were catastrophic in the area which has for decades suffered high jobless rates.
